newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Baht gains from offshore squeeze.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Baht gains from offshore squeeze.

text.p: The Thai baht continued its upward march in offshore markets on Monday as players were forced to sell dollars to cover their short baht positions due to prohibitively expensive funding costs in the swap market.
"If the swaps are too expensive, there's no point holding the currency so they're selling dollars and buying back the baht," a Singapore-based dealer said.
"They have to get out of the positions. Otherwise, the funding is going to cost them a few hundred percent every day," he added.

The baht was quoted at 24.840/24.850 to the dollar at 0400 GMT in offshore markets against 24.950/25.050 late on Friday. In the domestic market, the baht was steady at 25.820/25.840 compared with 25.800/25.850 late on Friday.
The Bank of Thailand (BOT) set the mid-rate at 25.81 per dollar against 25.80 on Friday.

The one-month baht/dollar swap premium was traded at 110/160 satangs per dollar in the offshore market versus 100/140 late on Friday. In the domestic market, the one-month swap premium was 20/30 satangs, unchanged from late on Friday, dealers said.
Before the central bank's measures created an informal two-tier foreign exchange market, the one-month swap premium was at around 6.00/10.00 satangs.

Bangkok dealers said a May 28 BOT circular asking financial institutions to suspend all forex swap deals that gave foreign partners access to baht funds, contained nothing new but it was the first time the central bank had put its directive in writing.
The Singapore dealer said the baht should not head much higher as it was already "grossly overvalued".
"If anything, dollar/baht should head back above the 25.0 level, but it's a matter of time," he added.
In Indonesia, the rupiah continued to firm as players focused on the country's sound fundamentals after a relatively smooth general election last week.
Dealers said the market was off to its usual slow Monday start, but forwards weakened on ample liquidity in the short end, with short-term swaps sliding below par.
A dealer in Singapore said capital inflows seemed to resume in the spot rupiah market after the election.
"The rupiah continues to strengthen regardless of its ample supply. Those are signs of capital inflows," the dealer said.
"We know where the market is heading. Each time we receive a call, we know which side to hit in a quiet market. Rates are drifting to the left," he added.
Spot rupiah was at 2,430.5/31.5 at 0400 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,431.5/32.0.
But many dealers remained cautious, awaiting the Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP)'s decision on Thursday on whether to accept the outcome of last week's poll.
The PPP has claimed there were widespread irregularities during the election in which the ruling Golkar party swept more than 74 percent of the votes, The PPP took nearly 23 percent.
The Malaysian ringgit weakened on early offshore dollar buying, but dealers said its fall was cushioned by domestic demand for the ringgit.
"Sydney bought up dollar/ringgit to around 2.5160 this morning, but it fell back when Malaysian trading started," a dealer at a Malaysian bank said.
Dealers said the ringgit could see fresh selling in London later in the day. "There has been a lot of selling out of London and the ringgit could again head for 2.5200," a European bank dealer said.
But he said fears of Bank Negara intervention should cap dollar/ringgit at that level after the central bank was rumoured to be checking rates at 2.5190/95 on Wednesday.
The ringgit was quoted at 2.5150/60 to the dollar at 0400 GMT against 2.5117/27 at the close of Kuala Lumpur on Friday.
-- Syed Azman in Kuala Lumpur (603-206 2323), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221 384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662) 652-0642 and Sonali Desai in Singapore (65-8703090)
